audit.title: CCIP Contract Interface Reference Documentation (TON)
audit.contentType: developer documentation / API reference index (version landing page)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Working: the `<Aside>` gives a self-contained scope statement an engine can lift verbatim. Weak: there's no one-sentence definition of "CCIP on TON" up top before the version list.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 5 clean headings, 1 H1, 0 level skips, sensible bullet chunks. No action needed beyond size, which is fine for an index.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak: measured 0 numerals in prose; only qualitative feature bullets ("configurable gas limits," "native GRAM fee payments") with no numeric limits, chain IDs, or version-date specifics.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak: 3 internal links, 0 external. No link to the CCIP conceptual overview, the TON docs, or a primary spec to anchor entity resolution.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Partial: the scope aside is quotable, but neither "CCIP" nor "TON Starter Kit" gets a crisp inline definition near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, dateModified/datePublished absent (head not captured — CLI should pass raw `<head>`). No freshness signal for an "unaudited" utilities claim that will age.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Not applicable in substance; an index page carries no code. Scored neutral, not penalized.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Partial: answers "what versions exist" and "does TON support token transfers." Missing "how do I send a CCIP message from TON," "TON supported chains," and error/symptom phrasings — those live in sub-pages but no signposting question-headings route to them.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; unambiguous, consistent product naming ("CCIP v1.6.0," "TON Starter Kit").

audit.summary: This is a thin (145-word) version-landing/index page whose job is to route readers to the CCIP v1.6.0 TON reference and to state platform scope. Its biggest strength is a crisp, liftable scope statement — "TON currently supports arbitrary message passing only. Token transfers are not yet supported." — that directly answers a common capability query. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability: no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no visible last-updated date were found, so agents get no structured trust signals. Honest verdict: appropriate as a hub, but under-optimized on metadata and on symptom/how-to query coverage; both are cheap, high-value fixes given the page's routing role.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `about: ["Chainlink CCIP","TON"]`, `version: "1.6.0"`, a canonical `https://docs.chain.link/ccip/api-reference/ton`, and a rendered "Last updated" date.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust, which agents weight when choosing a source to cite.

recommendations.title: Lead with a one-sentence canonical definition
recommendations.where: immediately under the H1, before "Available Versions"
recommendations.issue: page opens into a version list with no self-contained "what is this"
recommendations.change: add e.g. "Chainlink CCIP on TON enables cross-chain arbitrary messaging between TON and EVM-based chains, with fees paid in native GRAM (nanoGRAM). Token transfers are not yet supported."
recommendations.why: a crisp first liftable sentence defends against parametric priors and gives engines a quotable capability summary.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to question headings that route to sub-pages
recommendations.where: new short section or reworded "Documentation Structure" bullets
recommendations.issue: concept-titled bullets ("Router Interface (sending messages and fee estimation)") miss how devs query
recommendations.change: phrase as questions linking to the v1.6.0 sub-docs: "How do I send a CCIP message from TON?", "How do I estimate CCIP fees on TON?", "What CCIP error codes does TON return?"
recommendations.why: symptom/how-to headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses, and turn this hub into an entry point.

recommendations.title: Add authoritative external/conceptual links
recommendations.issue: 0 external links; "CCIP" and "TON" are unanchored entities
recommendations.change: link "CCIP" to the CCIP conceptual overview and "TON" to official TON documentation; keep the internal `/ccip/api-reference/ton/v1.6.0` links.
recommendations.why: inline links to canonical concept pages improve entity resolution and citation credibility.

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to the feature bullets
recommendations.issue: measured 0 numerals in prose; "Configurable gas limits" is vague
recommendations.change: state the release date, the fee-token denomination precision (nanoGRAM = 1e-9 GRAM), and any default/max gas limit or supported EVM chain count where known.
recommendations.why: quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes for generative retrieval and citation.

antiPatterns: Stale/undated content risk: an "unaudited TypeScript utilities" claim with no dateModified will silently age. No keyword stuffing, fluff, or unresolved cross-references detected.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced on-page — good site-level signal; ensure this URL is listed in it and in the sitemap.
Head metadata could not be verified from the supplied content; run the CLI with raw `<head>` passthrough to confirm canonical/schema state before acting on the metadata score.
Site-level: ensure the version hub is internally linked from the CCIP API reference overview so it inherits authority (canonical-hub pattern).
